title: Input and Pesticide Compliance: Verify Before Use

content.overview: Input compliance is a verification workflow. Before use, the learner must identify the exact product and label, confirm the intended crop/site/use, identify worker-protection requirements, verify any jurisdiction-specific restrictions, prepare required controls and preserve enough evidence for the decision to be reconstructed later.

vocabulary.definition: The crop, site, rate, method, timing and other conditions authorized or directed by a product label.
Entry into a treated area after application, subject to applicable label, worker-protection and regulatory restrictions.
A traceable record of product identity, date/time, location, use, responsible person and other information required by law or procedure.
The specific label, rule, guidance or policy version relied on for a decision.
A condition that requires the task to pause because authorization, controls or required information are missing or unclear.

sections.title: Confirm the exact product and current label
sections.body: Similar product names, concentrations or formulations are not interchangeable. Verification should start with the container/product identity and the current label/SDS associated with that exact product.

sections.title: Crop/site/use must be explicitly supported
sections.body: A product being sold for gardens, agriculture or 'organic' use does not establish that the intended cannabis/hemp crop, site or method is authorized. Verify the label and the applicable jurisdiction before application.

sections.title: Worker-protection duties are part of the decision
sections.body: PPE, decontamination, training, application restrictions, notification/reentry and emergency assistance can change whether and how a task may proceed. These are not optional add-ons after the product decision.

sections.title: Preserve the evidence used
sections.body: Keep the source/version information used for the decision, plus the application record required by law or facility procedure. Historical records should not silently inherit a newer label or rule version.

sections.title: Define stop conditions before work starts
sections.body: If the label is missing, product identity is uncertain, worker protections are unavailable, crop/site authorization is unclear or jurisdiction-specific restrictions have not been resolved, the correct action is to stop and escalate rather than improvise.

workedExamples: A forum recommends a product for cannabis, but the current label does not clearly support the planned crop/site use. The recommendation is not treated as authorization.

Two containers have similar brand names but different active-ingredient concentrations. The worker verifies the exact label/SDS for the product in hand rather than relying on last season's instructions.
A label version changes between seasons. Historical application records preserve the version used at the time so later review is reproducible.
A required decontamination station is not available. Work does not begin even though the product itself appears authorized.
commonMistakes: Assuming natural or organic means unrestricted.
Using a label for a similar but different product.
Treating a vendor page as the controlling label.
Checking crop/site authorization but ignoring worker protection.
Failing to preserve the version of the label/rule used.
Continuing when a stop condition is present.
content.practicalApplication: Complete a pre-use compliance checklist for a supplied label/SDS and hypothetical jurisdiction. Record exact product identity, label version, crop/site/use, worker protections, reentry/notification, emergency information, jurisdiction-specific restrictions, required records and stop conditions.
content.summary: Responsible input use is evidence-driven. Product identity, label authorization, worker protection, jurisdiction and traceable documentation must all agree before application.

blocks.title: Input-verification matrix
rows: Which source/version did we rely on?

blocks.title: Same brand, different formulation
blocks.setting: A worker recognizes the brand name and starts using last season's mixing and PPE notes. The current container has a different concentration and label revision.
options: Continue because the brand is the same
Stop and verify the exact current label/SDS and requirements
Ask a coworker what they remember
blocks.answer: Stop and verify the exact current label/SDS and requirements.
blocks.feedback: Product identity and current source version must match the task. Familiarity is not a substitute for verification.

blocks.title: Pre-use compliance record
blocks.instructions: Review a training product packet and jurisdiction scenario.
prompts: Confirm exact identity and label revision.
List all stop conditions and escalation questions.
